source_limitations: Entries were checked against publisher/institutional pages and author-hosted material, not all original full texts. They are candidate arguments, not validated causal estimates or novelty findings.

sources.title: Days of Action or Restraint? How the Islamic Calendar Impacts Violence
sources.authors: Michael J. Reese; Keven G. Ruby; Robert A. Pape
sources.scope_limited_finding: Publisher abstract reports decreases on important Islamic holidays and no systematic increase associated with any Islamic holiday, including Ramadan.
sources.relevance: Direct evidence on own-constituency holiday restraint; not evidence of interstate war onset.
sources.verification: publisher abstract checked; original methods/results pages not independently audited

sources.title: Religion and terrorism: Evidence from Ramadan fasting
sources.authors: Roland Hodler; Paul A. Raschky; Anthony Strittmatter
sources.outcome: terrorist attacks and public support for terrorism
sources.holiday_exposure: Ramadan fasting intensity from daylight hours
sources.scope_limited_finding: Published abstract reports longer fasting daylight hours reduce support for terrorism and are associated with fewer terrorist attacks, particularly operationally difficult attacks.
sources.relevance: A possible audience-support and operational-cost mechanism; not a direct test of opponent surprise.
sources.verification: publisher abstract checked; full text not independently audited

sources.title: The Impact of Public Holidays on Insurgent Attacks: The Case of Thailand
sources.authors: Chris Chinda; Cigdem Unal; Zoe Marchment; Paul Gill
sources.outcome: daily insurgent attacks in southern Thailand
sources.holiday_exposure: Islamic, Buddhist, and secular Thai public holidays
sources.scope_limited_finding: Authors report increases on Islamic holidays and decreases on Buddhist and public holidays in their southern Thailand sample.
sources.relevance: Directly tests heterogeneous effects by holiday type; explicitly challenges any universal own-holiday-restraint rule.
sources.verification: open-access article and abstract located; comprehensive methods/results audit pending

sources.title: Sacred Time and Religious Violence: Evidence from Hindu-Muslim Riots in India
sources.holiday_exposure: religious ritual calendars and incompatible ritual observances
sources.scope_limited_finding: Publisher abstract argues ritual incompatibility between groups helps explain increased riot risk at sacred times.
sources.relevance: Directly relevant to holiday-triggered communal riots; NOT evidence of interstate military attack timing.
sources.verification: publisher abstract checked; full methods/results audit pending

sources.title: Religious Riots and Electoral Politics in India
sources.outcome: communal riots, with electoral consequences studied using an instrument
sources.holiday_exposure: Hindu festival falling on a Muslim holy Friday
sources.scope_limited_finding: Authors report higher riot probability when a Hindu festival falls on Friday, using calendar-based variation as an instrument in their electoral-effects design.
sources.relevance: Valuable calendar-based design inspiration, but not a study of interstate war onset.
sources.verification: article abstract and design description checked; identification validity not independently assessed

sources.title: Introducing the ETH/PRIO Civil Conflict Ceasefire Dataset
sources.holiday_exposure: holiday stated as purpose of the ceasefire arrangement
sources.scope_limited_finding: The dataset explicitly codes arrangements whose stated purpose is a holiday; its existence does not establish that holidays cause truces or that unannounced violence pauses are formal ceasefires.
sources.relevance: Direct measurement resource for negotiated holiday ceasefires, a distinct outcome.
sources.verification: journal methods/description and ETH dataset description checked; codebook data extraction pending

sources.title: The Rational Timing of Surprise
sources.outcome: strategic timing of the use of surprise
sources.scope_limited_finding: Analyzes timing incentives concerning surprise; no direct empirical result about holidays should be attributed to this paper.
sources.relevance: Potential formal-theory input for opportunity versus defensive anticipation, NOT direct evidence on holiday conflict effects.
sources.verification: journal article and author-hosted manuscript identified; full model not independently audited
